title: Visible history, CLI and MCP
steps: Open Garden plan, then ⌘⇧P → Show history of this note. Gardener and Planner made four changes after the seed; one is labelled “Spring plan”.
Click a change to see what it did. ⌘-click a second one (or Shift-click a range): the diff shows what they did together, and a change you skip in between is left out, as separate runs.
With the history panel focused: j and k move, Space or x toggles a change, Enter shows just that one.

Select one of Planner's changes and press Revert this change: only that change is undone, later edits stay. Revert two changes that touch the same line in the wrong order and it says which couldn't be reverted and why.
On a run, Restore to before puts the note back as it was before those changes, as a new change you can undo.
On “Spring plan”, Open shows the note as it was then, read-only in a tab; Changes since shows the diff with now, and Restore this version puts it back.
Add label… (in the panel, the tab menu, or ⌘⇧P) names the note as it is now. The label shows in the history list, and lives in `.common-ink/labels.json` (⌘P), so its own history says who added it.
Set the author filter to Gardener and press Undo all: both edits go, as one change each by you. Redo on an undone change puts it back.

From a terminal in a checkout: `COMMON_INK_URL=<this Preview> bin/common-ink history`, `bin/common-ink cat 'Garden plan.md'`, `echo hi | bin/common-ink write Hello.md`. The CLI writes as the agent CLI, working for you.

Add `<this Preview>/mcp?agent=Claude` as an HTTP MCP server in an MCP client. Its tools include list_files, read_file, write_file, history, diff, undo, restore, labels and add_label, and its changes show up in history as Claude's.
